facts.statement: Amurosaurus was first described and named by Russian paleontologists Yuri Bolotsky and Sergei Kurzanov in 1991.
facts.quote: Russian paleontologists Yuri Bolotsky and Sergei Kurzanov first described and named this dinosaur in 1991.

facts.statement: The genus name Amurosaurus combines the Amur River with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Amur River and the Greek word sauros ("lizard").

facts.statement: All Amurosaurus fossils come from a single bonebed discovered in 1984 near Blagoveschensk in the Amur Oblast of Russia.
facts.quote: All fossils of Amurosaurus have been recovered from a single bonebed locality, discovered in 1984 within the city limits of Blagoveschensk in the Amur Oblast of far eastern Russia.

facts.statement: Amurosaurus lived in eastern Asia during the Late Cretaceous, between 70 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Amurosaurus (; "Amur lizard") is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur found in Late Cretaceous (70 to 66 million years ago) deposits of what is now eastern Asia.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Udurchukan Formation, the oldest geologic formation in the Tsagayan Group of far eastern Russia and northeastern China.
facts.quote: This bonebed is found in the Udurchukan Formation, the oldest geologic formation in the Tsagayan Group of far eastern Russia and northeastern China.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 million years ago.
facts.quote: This formation is thought to belong to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period, and was deposited about 68 million years ago, or just prior to the Lancian faunal stage of North America.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a left maxilla and a left dentary from the same individual.
facts.quote: The holotype, or original specimen, consists of only a maxilla (upper jaw bone), and a dentary (lower jaw bone), both from the left side of the same individual.

facts.statement: Recent descriptions of additional material have made Amurosaurus the most abundant and completely known dinosaur from Russia.
facts.quote: This other material was described more recently, making Amurosaurus the most abundant and completely known Russian dinosaur.

facts.statement: Abundant theropod teeth and toothmarks on the bones suggest predation or scavenging by carnivores.
facts.quote: Theropod teeth are also abundant, and there are many toothmarks on the bones, made by predators or scavengers.

facts.statement: The genus Sahaliyania is considered a junior synonym of Amurosaurus.
facts.quote: Sahaliyania (from "black" in Manchu, a reference to the Amur/Heilongjiang River), is a junior synonym of Amurosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2022 reassessment confirmed that Sahaliyania is a junior synonym of Amurosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2022 article reassessed Sahaliyania and considered it a junior synonym of Amurosaurus.

facts.statement: Amurosaurus is distinguished by unique skull features and a sigmoidal (S-shaped) ulna.
facts.quote: Amurosaurus is characterized by many autapomorphies, or unique features, of the skull, as well as the sigmoidal shape of the ulna (the lower arm bone) when viewed from the front or side.

facts.statement: Although the crest bones are missing, modified skull roof bones suggest Amurosaurus likely had a hollow crest like other lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Most other known lambeosaurines have hollow crests on the top of their skulls, and although the bones that would make up such a crest are unknown for this dinosaur, the bones on the roof of the skull are modified to support one, so it can be assumed that Amurosaurus was crested as well.

facts.statement: Amurosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 8 meters and a weight of 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: It has been estimated at 8 m in length and about 3 MT in weight.

facts.statement: As a hadrosaurid, Amurosaurus was a herbivore.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Amurosaurus would have been herbivorous.

facts.statement: Amurosaurus had a high encephalisation quotient, suggesting it likely engaged in complex social behaviors.
facts.quote: Amurosaurus had a high encephalisation quotient relative to sauropods and ceratopsians although lower than that of theropods, as would be expected of an animal that likely engaged in complex social behaviours.

facts.statement: A 2020 study of Sahaliyania material helped refine the classification of Amurosaurus.
facts.quote: The 2020 osteological description of the material previously constituting the distinct genus Sahaliyania found the latter genus to be a synonym of Amurosaurus, allowing its newly restudied material to contribute to more robust tests of the classification of Amurosaurus.

facts.statement: Adult fossils are rare, but estimates suggest Amurosaurus could reach 8 meters in length and weigh 3 tons.
facts.quote: Los huesos fósiles de adultos son raros, pero se estima que pudieron llegar a medir hasta 8 metros de largo y un peso de 3 toneladas.

facts.statement: This duck-billed dinosaur is the best-known dinosaur from Russia.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio de pico de pato es el dinosaurio mejor conocido de Rusia.

facts.statement: Russian paleontologists Yuri Bolotsky and Sergei Kurzanov discovered and described Amurosaurus in 1991.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos rusos Yuri Bolotsky and Sergei Kurzanov descubrieron y describieron este animal en 1991.

facts.statement: The name Amurosaurus comes from the Amur River and the Greek word saurus, meaning lizard.
facts.quote: El nombre viene del Río Amur y la palabra griega saurus que significa lagartija.

facts.statement: The Amur River, located on the border between Russia and China, is near the site where the dinosaur's remains were found.
facts.quote: El Amur (llamado Heilongjiang o "Río del Dragón Negro" en chino) se ubica en la frontera entre Rusia y China, y está cerca del depósito donde se encontraron los restos del dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Only one species, A. rabinini, is known, named in honor of Russian paleontologist Anatoly Rabinin who led the first Russian expeditions to the Amur region in 1916 and 1917.
facts.quote: Existe sólo una especie conocida, llamada A. rabinini, en honor del paleontólogo ruso Anatoly Rabinin quien condujo la primera expedición rusa a los yacimientos en la región de Amur en 1916 y 1917.

facts.statement: Amurosaurus fossils were recovered from a single paleontological site discovered in 1984 near the city of Blagoveschensk in the Amur Oblast of the Russian Far East.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Amurosaurus fueron recobrados de un solo sitio paleontológico, descubierto en 1984 en los límites de la ciudad de Blagoveschensk en el óblast de Amur del lejano oriente ruso.

facts.statement: The formation dates to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 74 to 66 million years ago, though there is some disagreement about the exact timing of deposition.
facts.quote: Esta formación pertenece al Maastrichtiense, último estrato del Cretácico superior, datado alrededor de 74 a 66 millones de años atrás, aunque haya un cierto desacuerdo cuando esta etapa fáunica en Udurchukan fuera depositada exactamente.

facts.statement: Sediments indicate an alluvial plain and river transported the fossils only a short distance, as evidenced by disarticulated and randomly ordered but well-preserved bones, including fragile skull elements.
facts.quote: Los sedimentos muestran una llanura aluvional y un río, que transportó los fósiles, pero solo una corta distancia, juzgando por los huesos desarticulados y ordenados aleatoriamente, pero bien preservados dentro de la cama de huesos, incluyendo elementos frágiles del cráneo.

facts.statement: While only a small section of the site has been studied, 90% of the remains found so far belong to lambeosaurines like Amurosaurus, mostly juveniles, with the rest belonging to other taxa such as the hadrosaurine Kerberosaurus.
facts.quote: Solamente una pequeña sección de la localización se ha estudiado, pero el 90% de los restos encontrados hasta ahora pertenecen a los lambeosáurinos como Amurosaurus, sobre todo jóvenes, con el resto perteneciendo a otras taxones, tales como el hadrosaurino Kerberosaurus.

facts.statement: Theropod teeth are abundant, and there are many tooth marks on the bones made by predators or scavengers.
facts.quote: Los dientes de terópodos son también abundantes, y hay muchas marcas de dientes en los huesos, hechos por depredadores o carroñeros.

facts.statement: The type specimen consists only of a maxilla and a dentary, both from the left side of the same individual.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, consiste solo en un maxilar (hueso superior de la boca) y un dentario (hueso inferior de la boca), ambos del lado izquierdo del mismo individuo.

facts.statement: However, most of the skull and postcranial skeleton bones have been collected from the bone bed of several distinct individuals.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la mayoría de los huesos del cráneo y esqueleto postcraneal han sido recogidos de la cama de huesos, de varios individuos distintos.

facts.statement: This material was described more recently, making Amurosaurus the most abundant and well-known dinosaur in Russia.
facts.quote: Este material fue descrito más recientemente, haciendo de Amurosaurus el dinosaurio ruso más abundante y mejor conocido de Rusia.

facts.statement: Due to the recent description of most of its unique features, in early 2006 Amurosaurus was included in a cladistic analysis placing it as a basal member of the hadrosaurid subfamily Lambeosaurinae, but more derived than Tsintaosaurus or Jaxartosaurus.
facts.quote: Debido a que la mayor parte de sus características únicas fueron descritas recientemente, a principios del 2006, Amurosaurus se lo ha incluido solamente en un análisis cladístico, que lo colocó como miembro basal de la subfamilia Lambeosaurinae de hadrosáuridos, pero más derivado que Tsintaosaurus o Jaxartosaurus.

facts.statement: All known basal lambeosaurines come from Asia, leading to the hypothesis that they originated there and later dispersed across the Bering Strait to North America.
facts.quote: Todos los lambeosaurinos basales conocidos provienen de Asia, lo que ha llevado a la hipótesis que los lambeosaurinos se originaron allí y para luego dispersarse a través del Estrecho de Bering a Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The two derived groups, the parasaurolophines and the lambeosaurines, developed later.
facts.quote: Los dos grupos derivados, los parasaurolofinis (Parasaurolophus, Charonosaurus) y los lambeosaurinis (Corythosaurus, Nipponosaurus) se desarrollaron más adelante.

facts.statement: Since members of both groups are found in North America and Asia, there must have been additional dispersal after their evolution, though the direction of that dispersal remains somewhat confusing.
facts.quote: Como se encuentran miembros de ambos grupos en Norteamérica y Asia, debe haber habido una dispersión adicional después de su evolución, aunque en qué dirección ocurrió esa dispersión es aún algo confuso.

facts.statement: The parent group of Amurosaurus is Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Amurosaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Amurosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Amurosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
